Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

if not conjunction

also but if not, if … not, and if not, failing that

classical

Phaedr. 4 epil. 7: sī nōn ingenium, certē brevitātem approbā
Varr. RR 1.11.2: sī nōn, quam proximē

sī nōn

sī with nōn before the word negated; alone after a first condition

Negates one word, not the whole condition (for that, nisi: see unless); also “if not”, “failing that”, after a first condition.

Other words

  • sīn (sīn minus, sīn aliter) — but if (not)

    conjunction: the second of two conditions, the other way · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.4.3: sī est spēs nostrī reditūs … sīn, ut ego metuō, trānsāctum est; Cic. Att. 1.2.1: sīn aliter acciderit, hūmāniter ferēmus

    After sī: “but if”. With the verb left out, sīn minus or sīn aliter, “but if not”.

  • sī minus — if not (then at least)

    sī with minus, the verb understood · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 3.7: sī minus sapientēs, at certē summā laude dignōs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 287

    “If not this, at least that”: Lewis & Short gives it as the same as sīn minus.

Examples

  • sī nōn ingenium, certē brevitātem approbā

    if not my talent, at least approve my brevityPhaedr. 4 epil. 7

  • vīlla aedificanda potissimum ut intrā saepta vīllae habeat aquam, sī nōn, quam proximē

    the farmhouse should above all be built with water inside its walls, or if not, as near as possibleVarr. RR 1.11.2

  • quem sī legēs, laetābor; sīn autem minus, habēbunt certē quō sē oblectent posterī

    if you read it, I shall be glad; but if not, those who come after will at least have something to enjoyPhaedr. 3 prol. 31–32

  • sī est spēs nostrī reditūs, eam cōnfīrmēs et rem adjuvēs; sīn, ut ego metuō, trānsāctum est, quōquō modō potes ad mē fac veniās.

    if there is hope of my return, strengthen it and help the cause; but if, as I fear, it is all over, come to me any way you can.Cic. Fam. 14.4.3

See also unless, if, otherwise, else.
